part.text:
Confirmed: no internet (DNS fails, direct IP is "Network unreachable"), and no local interpreter or image tool (no Python/Node/Perl, no ImageMagick/Graphviz/PlantUML/Java). The only viable way to produce image files here is to generate **SVG directly** as text — which the user explicitly allowed ("one PNG (or SVG) per view").

I verified the model's semantics via the Structurizr export. The workspace has exactly **one view** — `SystemContext` — which (correctly, per C4) shows the **Patron** person and the **Library** software system, with the HTTPS relationship. Containers are internal to the system and not shown in a context view.

Your workspace defines **one view** (`SystemContext`), so there's one image file:

- **`/work/SystemContext.svg`** — the System Context view for the *Library* system

It shows the C4 context-level picture (verified against the Structurizr export of your DSL):
- **Patron** — `[Person]` — "Borrows books at the library."
- **Library** — `[Software System]` — "Manages books and loans."
- Relationship: **Patron → Library** — "Browses the catalogue through" `[HTTPS]`

The two containers (*Catalog Web App*, *Circulation Service*) are intentionally **not** shown — in a System Context view they're internal to the system. They'd appear on a Container view, which your DSL doesn't define yet.

This environment has **no internet** (DNS/network unreachable) and **no rendering toolchain** (no PlantUML, Java, Graphviz, Python, or Node), so I couldn't run the usual Structurizr → PlantUML → image pipeline. Instead I generated the SVG **directly as text**, styled to match C4 conventions (standard C4 colors, arrowhead, title, legend). It's a valid, self-contained SVG you can open in any browser or image viewer.
